extraction.Name: Millie Richards
extraction.Cancelled: The patent has not been canceled.
extraction.Refused/Protested: It was accepted with mental protest but was not recorded in the county.
extraction.Recorded patent: The patent was received by mail in September and was receipted for; not recorded in the county.
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: The land was mortgaged and one year later was sold.
extraction.Buyer: Mortgaged to J. D. Cordier of Pine Ridge and later sold to A. Baker
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: The land was sold because the debt and taxes were due and I could not raise the money to pay it. My property was mortgaged and it was due and taxes were due and I had no earning capacity so had to sell it for what I could get.
extraction.Occupation/Income: I have no way of making a living and depend solely on my husband who is sixty-nine years old, very poor eye site and has practically no earning capacity.
extraction.NOTES: Received $2300 for the land but the mortgage, taxes and interest amounted to about $800 and only $1500 was actually received. Sound of mind, not strong physically, financial condition is poor. Has no land, property, or money. No one depends upon her for support. An interpreter was present at the swearing. Document references District Superintendent. Land passed out of possession after one year. | CROSS-ROUTING PATTERN 2026-04-28: This record is one of 5 in the pine_ridge_* directory where the original Sonnet text-extraction captured a non-Pine-Ridge value in Tribe/Reservation. Source review and BLM cross-reference confirmed all 5 are Pine Ridge allottees who were living OFF-RESERVATION when they gave their affidavit/questionnaire testimony. The Tribe field had captured residence/sworn-at location rather than the allotment's tribal origin. Pattern documented as a systematic extraction-failure mode to be aware of in the rest of the corpus.
